title: Add canary rollout controller for Optimization Config (progressive apply + pause/resume)
author: Benji Okafor
description:
Context: Optimization Config changes (batching heuristics, cache toggles, quantization profiles) have caused production regressions and mis-scoped rollouts (see SUP-18503). As part of the Safe Apply + Rollback project, we need a first-class controller that can progressively apply a config version to a target scope and gate progression on health signals, with the ability to pause/resume and handle failures deterministically.

What this PR adds: (1) Canary rollout controller service inside the control plane that orchestrates staged apply for Optimization Config versions (tenant/model/region scope) using percent-based shards. (2) Pause/resume/cancel APIs and state machine persistence so rollouts survive process restarts. (3) Failure handling that stops progression, records the reason, and leaves the system in a safe paused state (no automatic rollback in this PR; rollback wiring is in ENG-4825/ENG-4823 follow-ups). (4) Metric tags + event annotations needed for SLO gates: tenant_id, model, region, config_version_id, rollout_id, shard.

High-level design: - Controller is a DB-backed state machine with a single active rollout per (tenant_id, model, region) scope enforced via unique constraint + optimistic concurrency. - Progression loop is driven by a worker (rollout_reconciler) that evaluates desired vs. actual and advances when gates are green for a configurable dwell window. - Sharding is deterministic based on worker shard_id modulo N (current N=100); canary_percentage maps to a shard set [0..pct-1]. - Gate evaluation is pluggable via a GateProvider interface; this PR implements basic latency/5xx hooks with a stubbed adapter (real rule library integration lands in PR-19933 + slo-toolkit PR-20023).

API surface (internal, Console will call these): - POST /internal/optimization-config/rollouts {scope, config_version_id, canary_percentage, dwell_seconds, gates} -> creates rollout - POST /internal/optimization-config/rollouts/{rollout_id}:pause - POST /internal/optimization-config/rollouts/{rollout_id}:resume - POST /internal/optimization-config/rollouts/{rollout_id}:cancel - GET /internal/optimization-config/rollouts/{rollout_id} - GET /internal/optimization-config/rollouts?scope=...

Operational notes: - Default dwell_seconds=300 for canary phase; gate evaluation window=5m with 1m step. - Controller only advances forward; any failure transitions to PAUSED (reason=GATE_FAILED|APPLY_FAILED|CONFLICT) and requires human resume/cancel. - This PR emits structured controller events to the rollout_events table; audit log emission for apply/promote/rollback is handled separately (ENG-4826 / PR-19941).

Testing: - Unit tests cover state transitions, pause/resume idempotency, and concurrency (two rollouts created for same scope). - Integration test spins up a fake runtime applier and injects gate failures to ensure the controller pauses and does not progress.

Rollout: - Feature-flagged behind optimization_config_rollouts_controller (off by default). - Will be enabled in staging for gameday scenarios before any production exposure.

Follow-ups: - Wire real SLO gate rules + dashboards (PR-19933, observability-pack PR-20012). - Wire rollback action as first-class controller transition (ENG-4825). - Quantization quality gate adapter (Applied ML) to block promote when eval regression is detected (ADR + upcoming PRs).

conversation:
Ethan Park (review): State machine looks good. Two asks: (1) Please clarify semantics when a rollout is paused mid-step (e.g., we’ve applied canary to 10% but haven’t evaluated gates yet). (2) Can we ensure we never create two ACTIVE rollouts for the same (tenant, model, region) even under retries/timeouts?

Benji Okafor (author): Added explicit PAUSED state with a frozen desired_shards snapshot; pause stops reconciler advancement but does not revert already-applied shards. Also added a unique constraint on scope_key where status IN (CREATED, RUNNING, PAUSED) enforced in store.Create(), and an idempotency_key optional field for client retries (documented in handler comments).

Sean Gallagher (review): From SRE side, we need consistent tags for alert correlation. Please include rollout_id + config_version_id on every apply attempt metric and log line (controller + applier). Also ensure failure reasons are enumerable and not free-form strings.

Benji Okafor (author): Added tags to metrics package + structured logger fields. Failure reasons are now an enum (GateFailed, ApplyFailed, Conflict, Cancelled) plus a separate diagnostic_message for debugging.

Jordan Lee (review): Authz: internal endpoints are fine but please wire policy checks for "optimization_change_operator" role now to avoid rework. Also, cancel should be idempotent and safe if already completed.

Benji Okafor (author): Added internal policy guard (temporary) mapping to the operator permission. Cancel endpoint is idempotent; if rollout is COMPLETED/FAILED/CANCELLED we return 200 with the current state.

Noah Patel (review): Concern: deterministic sharding based on worker shard_id is good, but runtime workers can churn. If shard_id assignment changes during rollout, canary set will drift. Any mitigation?

Benji Okafor (author): Good call. In this PR we bind rollout shards to a stable "apply_target_id" provided by runtime (currently model-worker logical ID, stable across restarts via etcd lease). Also added a guard to block progression if >5% of targets are "unknown" over the last window (prevents advancing during heavy churn).

Chloe Martin (review): Console will want to display status text + next step. Can you add a computed "progress" summary (phase, canary %, gate status, last_transition_at)?

Benji Okafor (author): Added RolloutStatusView in the handler response with phase, canary_percentage, gate_summary, last_transition_at, and last_error_reason. (Console-specific UX fields are minimal; more can be added later.)

Buildkite (CI): controlplane integration failed initially due to flaky time window assertions in gate evaluator.

Benji Okafor (author): Fixed tests to use a fake clock and widened the window boundaries. Re-ran integration; now green.

Ethan Park (final): Approved after the unique constraint + idempotency key changes. Please ensure follow-up task exists for hooking real SLO gates + dashboard.

Benji Okafor (author): Added follow-up to ENG-4827 and linked PR-19933 in description.
testing: Unit: rollout_state_machine_test covers transition legality (CREATED->RUNNING->PAUSED->RUNNING->COMPLETED, plus failure paths). Unit: rollout_concurrency_test simulates dual create calls and asserts single active rollout for same scope_key. Integration: optimization_config_rollouts_gate_failure_test runs reconciler with fake runtime applier; injects 5xx gate regression and asserts controller transitions to PAUSED with reason=GateFailed and does not advance shard set. Manual: started rollout in staging (tenant=dev-infra, model=llama-3.1-8b, region=us-east-1) with canary=5%, verified pause/resume endpoints and that apply attempts are annotated with rollout_id.
release_notes: Internal: Adds Optimization Config canary rollout controller with pause/resume/cancel.
Adds rollout_id/config_version_id metric tags for rollout correlation.
rollout_plan: Staging: enable optimization_config_rollouts_controller for internal tenant only; run gameday scenarios with synthetic gate failures; verify dashboards annotate rollout_id. Production: keep flag off until Console UI + audit events + rollback endpoint are available; then enable for selected Hosted/Dedicated accounts with SRE on-call coverage.
security_notes: Endpoints are /internal and gated by RBAC policy stub for optimization change operator. No customer-visible surface in this PR. Audit log emission is explicitly deferred to PR-19941/ENG-4826.
dependencies: Pairs with PR-19933 (gate hooks) for real SLO evaluation and with PR-19915/PR-19918 (runtime apply transaction + idempotency).
